literal: beautiful · not · able to · take in
natural: Too many beautiful things to take in

meaning.en: So many beautiful things that one cannot take them all in.
meaning.zh: 美好的东西太多，一时接受不完（欣赏不过来）。

examples.zh: 展览上的瓷器件件精美，真是美不胜收。
examples.en: Jiuzhaigou in autumn is a riot of colour — breathtaking at every turn.

examples.zh: 展览上的瓷器件件精美，令人美不胜收。
examples.en: Every piece of porcelain at the exhibition is exquisite — almost too much beauty to take in.

usage.en: Predicate. About scenery and artworks. 胜 is shèng (can bear).
usage.zh: 多作谓语，多形容风景、艺术品。

natural: Good at the start and good at the end

meaning.en: To do something well from beginning to end; to see things through.
meaning.zh: 做事有好的开头，也有好的结尾。

examples.zh: 做事要善始善终，不能虎头蛇尾。
examples.en: Finish what you start — don't let things fizzle out.

examples.zh: 离职前，她把手头工作都交接清楚，善始善终。
examples.en: Before leaving, she handed over all her work properly, seeing things through to the end.

story.en: Zhuangzi speaks of the sage who "is good with youth and good with age, good with the beginning and good with the end" (善夭善老，善始善终).
story.zh: 《庄子·大宗师》："善夭善老，善始善终。"

date.zh: 战国中期 · 前4—前3世纪

usage.en: Predicate. Often advice about work and duties.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常用于劝勉。

natural: Branches thick and leaves lush

meaning.en: Luxuriant and flourishing; also a thriving family or organisation.
meaning.zh: 枝叶繁密茂盛。也比喻家族兴旺或事业发展。

examples.zh: 院子里的老槐树枝繁叶茂。
examples.en: The old locust tree in the courtyard is in full leaf.

examples.zh: 经过几十年发展，这家企业已枝繁叶茂。
examples.en: After decades of growth, the company is thriving.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive. Literal (trees) or figurative (families, businesses).
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，可实指树木，也比喻家族、事业。

natural: Guard against small beginnings, block gradual growth

meaning.en: To nip something in the bud; to stop bad things while they are still small.
meaning.zh: 在错误或坏事刚冒头时就加以制止，不让它发展。

equivalents: a stitch in time saves nine

examples.zh: 对孩子的坏习惯要防微杜渐。
examples.en: Nip children's bad habits in the bud.

examples.zh: 反腐败必须防微杜渐，从小事抓起。
examples.en: Fighting corruption means stopping it early, starting with small things.

story.en: The minister Ding Hong warned the emperor about a powerful family: "if you correct government and take responsibility, block the gradual and guard against the sprouts" (杜渐防萌), disaster can be avoided.
story.zh: 丁鸿上书："若敕政责躬，杜渐防萌，则凶妖销灭，害除福凑矣。"

usage.en: Predicate. Formal; common in discipline, safety and anti-corruption contexts.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常用于纪律、安全、反腐。

synonyms: 勿以恶小而为之，勿以善小而不为

natural: Sweat streaming down and soaking the back

meaning.en: Drenched in sweat (from heat, hard work or fear).
meaning.zh: 汗水流得满背都是。形容出汗很多，也形容极度惶恐或惭愧。

examples.zh: 大热天搬家，大家都汗流浃背。
examples.en: Moving house on a hot day, everyone was sweating buckets.

examples.zh: 想到差点酿成大祸，他吓得汗流浃背。
examples.en: Realising he'd nearly caused a disaster, he broke out in a cold sweat.

story.en: When the powerful Cao Cao came before Emperor Xian, the emperor rebuked him; Cao left terrified, and "looking about, his sweat streamed down and soaked his back" (顾左右，汗流浃背).
story.zh: 曹操见汉献帝，献帝出言责备，"操出，顾左右，汗流浃背，自后不敢复朝请"。

usage.en: Predicate or complement. Today mostly heat and exertion; originally fear. Internet slang uses it jokingly for being stunned.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、补语。现多指热、累，原指惶恐。网络上也戏用。

natural: Putting the roots and branches upside down

meaning.en: To put the unimportant before the important; to get one's priorities backwards.
meaning.zh: 把根本的和枝节的位置颠倒了。比喻把主次、轻重弄颠倒了。

equivalents: put the cart before the horse
miss the forest for the trees

examples.zh: 为了买名牌而不吃饭，这是本末倒置。
examples.en: Skipping meals to buy designer labels is putting the cart before the horse.

examples.zh: 学校只抓考试不抓品德，有本末倒置之嫌。
examples.en: A school that focuses only on exams and not on character risks getting its priorities backwards.

usage.en: Predicate. Common criticism in essays and commentary.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常用于批评。

synonyms: 抓了芝麻丢西瓜——主次不分

natural: Pouring oil on the fire

meaning.en: To make things worse; to add fuel to the fire.
meaning.zh: 往火上倒油。比喻使人更加愤怒或使事态更加严重。

examples.zh: 他正在气头上，你别再火上浇油了。
examples.en: He's already furious — don't add fuel to the fire.

examples.zh: 一些不实报道对紧张局势火上浇油。
examples.en: Some false reports poured oil on an already tense situation.

usage.en: Predicate. Very common in speech.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，口语常用。

natural: Cut out a passage and take the meaning you want

meaning.en: To quote out of context; to distort meaning by selective quoting.
meaning.zh: 不顾全篇文章或谈话的内容，孤立地取其中一段或一句的意思。

examples.zh: 媒体断章取义，歪曲了他的本意。
examples.en: The media quoted him out of context and twisted his meaning.

examples.zh: 读书要读完整，不能断章取义。
examples.en: Read the whole text — don't take bits out of context.

story.en: In ancient diplomacy, envoys recited lines from the Book of Songs to make points. One official admitted: "when reciting poems I cut out stanzas and take what I need" (赋诗断章，余取所求焉).
story.zh: 《左传》："赋诗断章，余取所求焉。"春秋时外交场合常截取《诗经》片段表达己意。

usage.en: Predicate or attributive. Criticises misquoting, especially in media and online.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，批评歪曲引用。

natural: Hard to go forward, hard to go back

meaning.en: In a dilemma; stuck with no good way forward or back.
meaning.zh: 前进和后退都很困难。比喻处境困难。

equivalents: between a rock and a hard place

examples.zh: 工作做到一半发现方向错了，真是进退两难。
examples.en: Realising halfway through that we'd gone the wrong way left us between a rock and a hard place.

examples.zh: 房价太高，买也不是，不买也不是，他陷入了进退两难的境地。
examples.en: House prices are so high he can't decide whether to buy — he's in a real dilemma.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive (进退两难的境地).
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语。

synonyms: 武大郎攀杠子——上不着天，下不着地
豆腐掉进灰堆里——吹不得打不得

natural: Correct one's faults and start anew

meaning.en: To mend one's ways and make a fresh start.
meaning.zh: 改正错误，重新做人。

examples.zh: 法律给了他改过自新的机会。
examples.en: The law gave him a chance to turn over a new leaf.

examples.zh: 他出狱后改过自新，开了一家小饭馆。
examples.en: After leaving prison he mended his ways and opened a small restaurant.

story.en: The girl Tiying pleaded with Emperor Wen to spare her father from mutilating punishment, since a mutilated man "may wish to correct his faults and renew himself, but has no way" (欲改过自新，其道无由也). The emperor abolished such punishments.
story.zh: 缇萦上书救父："虽欲改过自新，其道无由也。"汉文帝因此废除肉刑。

usage.en: Predicate or attributive (改过自新的机会).
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语。

natural: Too anxious to succeed

meaning.en: Impatient for quick success.
meaning.zh: 急于取得成功。

examples.zh: 学外语不能急于求成，要循序渐进。
examples.en: You can't rush learning a language — take it step by step.

examples.zh: 急于求成往往欲速则不达。
examples.en: Being too eager for quick success often backfires.

usage.en: Predicate. Usually advice against haste.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常用于劝诫。

natural: A hundred setbacks without bending

meaning.en: Indomitable; unbowed by repeated setbacks.
meaning.zh: 无论受到多少次挫折都不退缩。形容意志坚强。

examples.zh: 他百折不挠，失败了十几次终于创业成功。
examples.en: He never gave up — after a dozen failures, his business finally took off.

examples.zh: 这部电影讲述了一个百折不挠的运动员的故事。
examples.en: The film tells the story of an indomitable athlete.

story.en: Cai Yong praised the minister Qiao Xuan for "bending under a hundred setbacks without yielding, a spirit that cannot be robbed of its principles" (有百折不挠，临大节而不可夺之风).
story.zh: 蔡邕《太尉乔玄碑》："有百折不挠，临大节而不可夺之风。"

usage.en: Attributive or predicate (百折不挠的精神). 挠 is náo.
usage.zh: 多作定语、谓语。"挠"读 náo。

natural: Diligent and never weary

meaning.en: Tirelessly diligent, especially in study or work.
meaning.zh: 勤奋努力，不知疲倦。

examples.zh: 这位老教授至今仍孜孜不倦地做研究。
examples.en: The old professor still does research tirelessly.

examples.zh: 他孜孜不倦地学习，终于考上了理想的大学。
examples.en: He studied tirelessly and finally got into his dream university.

usage.en: Usually adverbial (孜孜不倦地学习/工作).
usage.zh: 多作状语。

natural: Its name heard far and near

meaning.en: Famous far and wide.
meaning.zh: 远近都知道它的名声，形容名声很大。

examples.zh: 景德镇的瓷器闻名遐迩。
examples.en: Jingdezhen porcelain is famous far and wide.

examples.zh: 这家百年老店闻名遐迩，每天都排长队。
examples.en: This century-old shop is renowned, with long queues every day.

usage.en: Predicate. About places, products and people. 遐 = far, 迩 = near.
usage.zh: 多作谓语。"遐"远，"迩"近。

natural: A disaster that goes over one's head

meaning.en: A catastrophe; total ruin.
meaning.zh: 水漫过头顶的灾难。比喻毁灭性的灾祸。

examples.zh: 这场金融危机给很多企业带来了灭顶之灾。
examples.en: The financial crisis was a catastrophe for many businesses.

examples.zh: 如果堤坝决口，下游村庄将遭受灭顶之灾。
examples.en: If the dam bursts, the villages downstream will be wiped out.

usage.en: Object of 遭受/带来/招致.
usage.zh: 常作"遭受、带来、招致"的宾语。

story.en: The Book of Changes, in the Great Excess hexagram, says "wading through water that goes over the head means misfortune" (过涉灭顶，凶). 灭顶, being submerged over the head, became the image of utter disaster.
story.zh: 《周易·大过》上六：“过涉灭顶，凶。”“灭顶”指水淹没头顶，后来比喻彻底的灾难。

natural: Winds in season and rains on time

meaning.en: Favourable weather for crops; good fortune.
meaning.zh: 风雨适时适量，适合农作物生长。也比喻太平。

examples.zh: 今年风调雨顺，粮食大丰收。
examples.en: The weather was kind this year, and there was a bumper harvest.

examples.zh: 春节时人们祈求新年风调雨顺、国泰民安。
examples.en: At Spring Festival people pray for good weather and peace in the new year.

usage.en: Predicate. Often paired with 国泰民安 in New Year wishes.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常与"国泰民安"连用。

natural: Settled by agreement, formed by custom

meaning.en: Established by common usage; accepted through long custom.
meaning.zh: 指事物的名称或社会习惯是由人们共同认定、长期实行而形成的。

examples.zh: 很多语言规则都是约定俗成的。
examples.en: Many language rules are simply established by usage.

examples.zh: 在这里，见面握手是约定俗成的礼节。
examples.en: Here, shaking hands when you meet is the accepted custom.

story.en: Xunzi argued that names have no inherent rightness: "they are fixed by agreement; once agreed and customary, they are called right" (约定俗成谓之宜).
story.zh: 《荀子·正名》："名无固宜，约之以命，约定俗成谓之宜。"

usage.en: Attributive or predicate. Common in discussions of language and customs.
usage.zh: 多作定语、谓语，常用于语言和习俗。

natural: Honest and clean in public service

meaning.en: Honest and incorruptible in public service.
meaning.zh: 廉洁不贪，奉行公事。

examples.zh: 干部应当廉洁奉公，不谋私利。
examples.en: Officials should serve with integrity and never seek personal gain.

examples.zh: 他当了三十年官，一直廉洁奉公。
examples.en: In thirty years in office, he was always incorruptible.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive. Formal; official and news language.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，用于公文、新闻。

antonyms: 孙大圣管蟠桃园——监守自盗

natural: Correct the root and clear the source

meaning.en: To tackle a problem at its root; a fundamental reform.
meaning.zh: 从根本上整顿，从源头上清理。

equivalents: get to the root of the problem

examples.zh: 解决食品安全问题，必须正本清源。
examples.en: Solving food safety problems means tackling them at the source.

examples.zh: 这篇文章对流行的误解进行了正本清源。
examples.en: The article sets the record straight on common misconceptions.

usage.en: Predicate. Formal; about reform or correcting misunderstandings.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，用于整顿改革或澄清误解。

natural: Relying on the sky for one's food

meaning.en: To depend on the weather (or luck) for one's livelihood.
meaning.zh: 依靠自然条件维持生活，多指农业生产受天气左右。也指听天由命。

equivalents: at the mercy of the weather

examples.zh: 过去农民靠天吃饭，遇上旱灾就没收成。
examples.en: Farmers used to be at the mercy of the weather — a drought meant no harvest.

examples.zh: 有了灌溉系统，这里不再靠天吃饭了。
examples.en: With an irrigation system, people here no longer depend on the weather.

usage.en: Predicate. Colloquial; also used about businesses that depend on luck or seasons.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，口语。也用于受季节、运气影响的行业。

natural: Each displays their magic powers

meaning.en: Each shows off their own special skills.
meaning.zh: 各自施展自己的本领。

equivalents: everyone pulls out their best tricks

examples.zh: 比赛中，各队各显神通，竞争激烈。
examples.en: In the contest each team showed what it could do, and the competition was fierce.

examples.zh: 为了吸引顾客，商家们各显神通。
examples.en: Shops are each pulling out their best tricks to attract customers.

usage.en: Predicate. From the image of the Eight Immortals crossing the sea (八仙过海，各显神通).
usage.zh: 多作谓语。常与"八仙过海"连用。

natural: Heart thumping, unable to settle

meaning.en: Nervous and uneasy; on edge.
meaning.zh: 心神极为不安。

examples.zh: 等待面试结果时，她忐忑不安。
examples.en: She had butterflies in her stomach while waiting for the interview results.

examples.zh: 第一次见女朋友的父母，他心里忐忑不安。
examples.en: Meeting his girlfriend's parents for the first time, he was on edge.

usage.en: Predicate. 忐忑 is tǎntè. Often 心里忐忑不安.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常用"心里忐忑不安"。

synonyms: 十五个吊桶打水——七上八下
一颗心悬在半天云里——上不着天，下不着地

natural: Not confined to one pattern

meaning.en: Not bound by convention; flexible and diverse.
meaning.zh: 不局限于一种规格或方式。

examples.zh: 公司不拘一格选人才，看能力不看学历。
examples.en: The company recruits unconventionally, looking at ability rather than degrees.

examples.zh: 他的写作风格不拘一格。
examples.en: His writing style is unconventional.

story.en: Gong Zizhen's poem calls on heaven: "I urge the Lord of Heaven to rouse himself again, and send down talent not confined to one pattern" (我劝天公重抖擞，不拘一格降人才).
story.zh: 龚自珍《己亥杂诗》："我劝天公重抖擞，不拘一格降人才。"

usage.en: Adverbial or predicate. Famous in the phrase 不拘一格降人才.
usage.zh: 多作状语、谓语，常引"不拘一格降人才"。

natural: A clever thought suddenly stirs

meaning.en: To have a sudden brainwave.
meaning.zh: 急忙中转了一下念头，想出了一个办法。

examples.zh: 他灵机一动，用手机当镜子照了照后面。
examples.en: He had a brainwave and used his phone as a mirror to look behind him.

examples.zh: 小明灵机一动，想出了一个好主意。
examples.en: Xiao Ming suddenly came up with a great idea.

usage.en: Predicate, often opening a clause. Very common in stories and school writing. In speech 一 is yí.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常用于叙述。作文常用。

literal: as if · not have · that · matter
natural: As if nothing had happened

meaning.en: As if nothing had happened; calm and unconcerned.
meaning.zh: 像没有那回事一样。形容遇事沉着镇静或不把事情放在心上。

examples.zh: 他打碎了花瓶，却若无其事地走开了。
examples.en: He broke the vase and walked off as if nothing had happened.

examples.zh: 心里很紧张，她却装作若无其事的样子。
examples.en: She was nervous inside but acted as if nothing was wrong.

usage.en: Adverbial or attributive. Can praise composure or criticise indifference.
usage.zh: 多作状语、定语，可褒可贬。
